title: Trump says immigration crackdown was 'too tough' and played part in midterms defeat
summary:
US President Donald Trump has said his immigration crackdown was "too tough", marking one of his clearest public retreats from a defining plank of his political agenda, following his party's drubbing in the midterm elections.
In an interview with CBS' 60 Minutes programme, Trump said he believed he deserved an "A plus" for drastically limiting illegal border crossings, but he had been politically "hurt" by sweeping deportations.
The president told 60 Minutes that immigration "both helped and hurt" his fellow Republicans in Tuesday's midterms.
Trump also said he'd "love to do something on immigration" with congressional Democrats, without offering details.
In a previous interview with 60 Minutes a year ago, a defiant Trump insisted his administraiton's immigration raids "haven't gone far enough".

title: Stephen Miller, Trump's new chief of staff, is the architect of his controversial immigration policies
summary:
Washington — Top Trump adviser Stephen Miller, who is set to take over the White House chief of staff role on Monday, has driven President Trump's most controversial immigration policies during both of his administrations.
Mr. Trump announced the staffing shake-up on Friday, calling Miller one of his "most trusted" advisers.
The move comes after Republicans suffered crippling losses in the midterm elections and as Democrats plan sweeping investigations into the administration's actions, including its immigration enforcement policies.
Miller also advocated penalizing legal immigrants who received public benefits and making it harder for them to obtain citizenship.
In Mr. Trump's second term, Miller pushed Immigration and Customs Enforcement to make at least 3,000 immigration arrests per day.

title: Marine Le Pen says "there is no discrimination in France" as she floats expelling immigrants who don't assimilate
summary:

"When you take in too many immigrants, you create the conditions for destabilizing your society," Le Pen said in an interview.
60 Minutes contributor Trevor Phillips told Le Pen that people in immigrant communities would argue the high immigrant unemployment rate is because of discrimination in France.
